svg.text: A. Fraction released versus time at temperature
BTCS model of one intact TRISO particle against the register's measurements; log scale; hours counted from reaching the test temperature
105 registered values drawn; none supports a comparison (context only)
65 registered values drawn; 17 support a comparison
64 registered values drawn; none supports a comparison (context only)
BTCS model, 1600 °C (marker colour is the test temperature)
BTCS model, 1700 °C (marker colour is the test temperature)
BTCS model, 1800 °C (marker colour is the test temperature)
Plus: independent analytical series, only where valid (criterion in the footnote)
Hollow square: model over the same 24 h-to-end window as a matrix-corrected value
Upper bound, model within it (WITHIN REPORTED UPPER BOUND)
Upper bound exceeded by the model (EXCEEDS REPORTED UPPER BOUND)
Hollow diamond: DATA INCOMPLETE, shown for scale, not a comparison
Grey cross: NOT DIRECTLY COMPARABLE context (muted)

Experimental values: Collin et al. (2016); IAEA (1997); IAEA (2012); Morris et al. (2016); Stempien et al. (2023). Digitised values carry the reading uncertainty of the register; the sources report no measurement

uncertainty for these rows, so no error bars are drawn. Compact values are not single-particle values. Rows with several times per compact are drawn at their own times; values without a time are drawn at the

registered end of test. Matrix-corrected values are releases over a window that starts at 24 h and ends at the plotted time, so they are drawn beside the model's value over the same window, not against the

cumulative curve. The model has no decay: every panel is the element, and the nuclides measured are listed in the panel. Analytical-series values are drawn only where the criterion holds: a value of the independent

analytical series is exported only where (1) the time is not earlier than the series' own minimum valid time (omitted modes below exp(-40) of their weight) and (2) the value exceeds the series' estimated absolute

accuracy (about 2.2e-16 over the smallest flux ratio of the shooting solution), and is positive; otherwise it is left empty Model: STRATO BTCS five-layer spherical finite difference, package version 1.0.1, commit

e56497225849397d8961bb0d032f885ecfb8fc0e; registered AGR1-B-M16 geometry; published heating-test diffusion coefficients chosen by the strato-data selection function (register sets C16-T2 and C16-BUF), evaluated at
the test temperature; kernel-only start; constant temperature; decay and generation are not in the solver. This is a numerical comparison, not an experimental validation.
